basis: Developmental disability defines syndrome; skeletal defects 2/2, great-artery transposition 1/2 and ptosis 1/3 support involvement, with small denominators.

decisions.ocular: involved: structural eyelid dysfunction (ptosis) in 1/3 assessed patients meets ~30%; estimate is uncertain because the denominator is small.

basis: Spotted-fever rickettsiosis directly infects vascular endothelium and causes small-vessel vasculitis; transient rash does not establish skin damage.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: endothelial infection and small-vessel vasculitis are defining tissue pathology of spotted-fever rickettsiosis.

basis: Generalized adipose loss defines a subcutaneous and metabolic disorder; associated fatty liver and diabetes are separately diagnosed diseases.

decisions.hepatic: none: fatty liver is common but is a separately diagnosed metabolic liver disease associated with lipodystrophy.

basis: Diffuse rigid skin defines disease; respiratory insufficiency occurs in 30-79% through restricted chest expansion, without established direct pulmonary injury.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory insufficiency in 30-79% reflects external restriction by rigid skin; direct lung, airway or pleural damage is not established.

basis: Inherited albumin synthesis disorder; subcutaneous lipodystrophy occurs in 30-79%, and osteoporosis is reported in 2/2 assessed patients; skeletal estimate is uncertain.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: osteoporosis represents bone damage reported in 2/2 assessed patients; supplied HPO frequency supports inclusion despite the small denominator.

basis: Metaphyseal dysplasia, adrenal hypoplasia and immunodeficiency define IMAGE-I; microcephaly alone does not establish brain dysfunction, and seizures occur in 3/15.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly (10/10) alone does not establish neurologic injury in this growth disorder; seizures occur in 3/15 (20%).

basis: Developmental impairment and optic nerve abnormalities characterize the syndrome; vertebral fusion and spinal/chest deformities occur in 30-79%; dental crowding alone is insufficient.

decisions.ocular: primary: optic nerve hypoplasia and strabismus are explicit defining features; optic atrophy and other ocular abnormalities occur in 30-79%.

basis: CBS deficiency with defining lens and skeletal disease (80-99%); neurologic involvement supported by ID in 14/14. Vascular disease (30-79%) omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: vascular disease qualifies at 30-79%, but the four-axis cap retains metabolic disease and more frequent ocular, skeletal and neurologic involvement.
decisions.neurologic: involved: intellectual disability in 14/14 and brain atrophy in 3/3 support common CNS injury; primary slots retain metabolic, lens and skeletal hallmarks.
decisions.ocular: primary: lens disease is a defining hallmark and ontology parent; ectopia lentis occurs in 80-99%.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: characteristic skeletal disease defines the syndrome; osteoporosis and recurrent fractures occur in 80-99%.

basis: Metabolic encephalopathy with defining microvascular injury; enteropathy causes chronic diarrhea in 6/8. Muscle pathology (11/11) omitted at cap; retinal tortuosity alone is insufficient.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: systemic microvascular injury is defining, producing acrocyanosis in 4/5 and petechiae in 5/8; these reflect intrinsic vascular pathology.

basis: Opioid toxicity directly depresses consciousness and central respiratory drive; apnea does not itself establish intrinsic pulmonary injury, and miosis is not ocular damage.

decisions.pulmonary: none: respiratory depression is caused by suppression of brain respiratory drive; the defining toxidrome does not establish direct lung or airway injury.
